answer.generated: Pooling operations reduce redundancy by extracting features from local regions of the input, making the representation invariant to small translations. This is because the same pooling function (commonly max-pooling) is applied across all spatial locations, so slight shifts in the input produce similar output patterns. By discarding some information through downsampling, pooling also helps focus on essential features, further promoting translation invariance.
